- First call (`tokenizer.nextToken()` for idAndDirection): guarded by `if (!tokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`
- Second call (`idAndDirTokenizer.nextToken()` for extIDStr): guarded by `if (!idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`
- Third call (`idAndDirTokenizer.nextToken()` for direction): guarded by `if (!idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) return null;`
- Fourth call (`tokenizer.nextToken()` for uriStr): guarded by `if (!tokenizer.hasMoreElements()) return null;`

Thus, all calls are preceded by checks that ensure at least one more token exists, so the `NoSuchElementException` is completely avoided in this context.
